newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues Offshore wins Asia-Pacific orders.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues Offshore wins Asia-Pacific orders.

text.p: Bouygues Offshore said on Thursday that it won two new contracts in the Asian-Pacific region.

As a leader of a consortium including P.T Gunanusa and Saipem, it landed a turnkey contract of 200 million francs to build and install two offshore platforms for Elf Petroleum Asia B.V. Brunei, the statement said. The share of Bouguyes Offshore is 80 million francs.

Bouygyes Offshore will be in charge of the management, engineering and procurement of the project. The delivery of the platforms, one of which is 2,500 tonnes and the other 3,230 tonnes, is set for March and the summer of 1998, respectively.

Bouygues Offshore also won a contract from American company Monsanto Enviro-Chem Systems to build and install a sulphuric acid plant in the Murrin Murrin project, 700 kilometers northeast of Perth, Australia.
The 100 million francs contract was awarded to Bouygues Offshore Australia.
The plant scheduled for delivery in March 1998 will be the largest sulfuric acid plant in the world with a daily production of 4,400 tonnes.
